translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gengyao came to court and received double-eyed peacock feathers, four-claw dragon rank patches, a yellow belt, a purple bridle, and gold coins.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加一等阿思哈尼哈番世職，令其子富襲。

translations.literal: In recounting merit he was granted the hereditary first-rank asihani han, which his son Fu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted the hereditary first-rank asihani han, which his son Fu inherited.

sentences.zh: 羹堯才氣凌厲，恃上眷遇，師出屢有功，驕縱。

translations.literal: Gengyao's talent was fierce and overbearing; relying on the emperor's favor and repeated military successes whenever his army went forth, he grew arrogant and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao's talent was fierce and overbearing. Relying on imperial favor and repeated victories in the field, he grew arrogant and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 行文諸督撫，書官斥姓名。

translations.literal: In documents to governors-general and governors he wrote their official titles and personal names.
translations.idiomatic: In correspondence to governors-general and governors he used their titles and personal names—a mark of disrespect.

sentences.zh: 請發侍衛從軍，使為前後導引，執鞭墜鐙。

translations.literal: He requested bodyguards sent with the army to serve as guides before and behind him, holding the whip and stirrup.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for bodyguards to accompany the army as guides and to hold his whip and stirrup.

sentences.zh: 入覲，令總督李維鈞、巡撫範時捷跪道送迎。

translations.literal: On coming to audience he ordered Governor-General Li Weijun and Governor Fan Shijie to kneel along the road to see him off and welcome him back.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court he ordered Governor-General Li Weijun and Governor Fan Shijie to kneel along the road to escort him.

sentences.zh: 至京師，行絕馳道。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital, he traveled the imperial roadway reserved for the emperor alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he traveled the roadway reserved for the emperor alone.

sentences.zh: 王大臣郊迎，不為禮。

translations.literal: When princes and grand ministers met him in the suburbs, he made no courtesy in return.
translations.idiomatic: When princes and grand ministers met him outside the city, he returned no courtesy.

sentences.zh: 在邊，蒙古諸王公見必跪，額駙阿寶入謁亦如之。

translations.literal: On the frontier, all Mongol princes and dukes had to kneel when they saw him; Imperial Son-in-law Abao likewise knelt when he came to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier every Mongol prince and duke knelt before him; even Imperial Son-in-law Abao knelt when he paid his respects.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦陝西布政使胡期恆及景灝可大用，劾四川巡撫蔡珽逮治，上即以授景灝，又擢期恆甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: He once recommended Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commissioner Hu Qiheng and Jinghao as men of great capacity, impeached Sichuan Governor Cai Ting and had him arrested for trial; the emperor immediately gave the post to Jinghao and also promoted Qiheng to governor of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Shaanxi Administration Commissioner Hu Qiheng and Jinghao for high office, impeached Sichuan Governor Cai Ting and had him arrested; the emperor gave Cai's post to Jinghao and made Qiheng governor of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 羹堯僕桑成鼎、魏之耀皆以從軍屢擢，成鼎布政使，之耀副將。

translations.literal: Gengyao's servants Sang Chengding and Wei Zhiyao were repeatedly promoted for following the army; Chengding became provincial administration commissioner, Zhiyao deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao's servants Sang Chengding and Wei Zhiyao were repeatedly promoted for following the army—Chengding to provincial administration commissioner, Zhiyao to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 羹堯請發將吏數十從軍，上許之。

translations.literal: Gengyao requested several dozen officers and officials sent with the army; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao asked that several dozen officers and officials accompany the army; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 覲還，即劾罷驛道金南瑛等，而請以從軍主事丁松署糧道。

translations.literal: On returning from audience he immediately impeached and dismissed courier-route officials including Jin Nanying, and requested that Ding Song, a director who had followed the army, act as grain-route commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from court he immediately impeached courier-route officials including Jin Nanying and asked that Ding Song, a director who had followed the army, act as grain-route commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上責羹堯題奏錯誤，命期恆率所劾官吏詣京師。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Gengyao for errors in his memorial headings and ordered Qiheng to lead the impeached officials to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached Gengyao for errors in his memorial headings and ordered Qiheng to bring the impeached officials to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，珽逮至，上召入見，備言羹堯暴貪誣陷狀，上特宥珽罪。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, when Ting was brought under arrest to the capital, the emperor summoned him for audience; he fully described Gengyao's violence, greed, and false impeachments, and the emperor specially pardoned Ting's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Ting was brought to the capital. The emperor summoned him, heard a full account of Gengyao's violence, greed, and false charges, and specially pardoned Ting.

sentences.zh: 二月庚午，日月合璧，五星聯珠，羹堯疏賀，用「夕惕朝乾」語，上怒，責羹堯有意倒置，諭曰：「羹堯不以朝乾夕惕許朕，則羹堯青海之功，亦在朕許不許之間而未定也。

translations.literal: On gengwu in the second month the sun and moon joined in splendor and the five planets aligned in a pearl string; Gengyao memorialized congratulations using the phrase "vigilant at evening, dry at morning" with the words inverted; the emperor was enraged, reproached Gengyao for deliberate inversion, and issued an edict saying: "If Gengyao does not grant that I am dry in the morning and vigilant at evening, then Gengyao's Qinghai merit also remains undecided between my granting it or not.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu in the second month the sun and moon joined and the five planets aligned; Gengyao sent a congratulatory memorial using the inverted phrase "vigilant at evening, dry at morning" instead of the proper "dry in the morning, vigilant at evening." The emperor was furious and said: "If Gengyao will not grant that I am vigilant morning and evening, then his Qinghai merit remains for me to grant or withhold as I choose.

sentences.zh: 」會期恆至，入見，上以奏對悖謬，奪官。

translations.literal: " When Qiheng arrived and was received in audience, because his memorial responses were perverse and absurd, he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: " When Qiheng arrived for audience, the emperor stripped him of office for absurd answers in memorials.

sentences.zh: 上命更定打箭爐外增汰官兵諸事，不用羹堯議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered reconsideration of matters of increasing and reducing troops beyond Dartsedo and did not use Gengyao's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reordered troop increases and reductions beyond Dartsedo and rejected Gengyao's proposals.

sentences.zh: 四月，上諭曰：「羹堯舉劾失當，遣將士築城南坪，不惜番民，致驚惶生事，反以降番复叛具奏。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the emperor issued an edict saying: "Gengyao's recommendations and impeachments were improper; he dispatched officers and soldiers to build a walled city at Nanping without regard for the tribes, causing alarm and incidents, yet memorialized that submitted tribes had rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the emperor said: "Gengyao's recommendations and impeachments were improper. He sent troops to build a walled city at Nanping without regard for the tribes, causing alarm and unrest, then reported that submitted tribes had rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 青海蒙古饑饉，匿不上聞。

translations.literal: Qinghai Mongols suffered famine, yet he concealed it and did not report upward.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai Mongols were starving, yet he concealed it from the throne.

sentences.zh: 怠玩昏憒，不可復任總督，改授杭州將軍。

translations.literal: Negligent, playful, and muddled, he could no longer be entrusted with the governor-generalship and was transferred to be general of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Negligent and muddled, he could no longer serve as governor-general and was made general of Hangzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 」而以鍾琪署總督，命上撫遠大將軍印。

translations.literal: " Zhongqi was appointed acting governor-general and ordered to present the Pacification General's seal.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongqi was made acting governor-general and ordered to present the Pacification General's seal.

sentences.zh: 羹堯既受代，疏言：「臣不敢久居陝西，亦不敢遽赴浙江，今於儀徵水陸交通之處候旨。

translations.literal: After Gengyao was replaced, he memorialized saying: "Your servant dares not remain long in Shaanxi, nor dare hurry to Zhejiang; I now wait for instructions at Yizheng, where land and water routes meet.
translations.idiomatic: After his replacement Gengyao wrote: "I dare not remain long in Shaanxi, nor hurry to Zhejiang; I now wait for instructions at Yizheng, where land and water routes meet.

sentences.zh: 」上益怒，促羹堯赴任。

translations.literal: " The emperor grew still angrier and urged Gengyao to proceed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor grew angrier still and ordered Gengyao to proceed to his post at once.

sentences.zh: 山西巡撫伊都立、都統前山西巡撫範時捷、川陝總督岳鍾琪、河南巡撫田文鏡、侍郎黃炳、鴻臚少卿單疇書、原任直隸巡撫趙之垣交章發羹堯罪狀，侍郎史貽直、高其佩赴山西按時捷劾羹堯遣兵圍郃陽民堡殺戮無辜，亦以讞辭入奏，上命分案議罪。

translations.literal: Shanxi Governor Yiduli, Banner Commander and former Shanxi Governor Fan Shijie, Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Yue Zhongqi, Henan Governor Tian Wenjing, Vice Minister Huang Bing, Court of State Ceremonial Vice Director Dan Choushu, and former Zhili Governor Zhao Zhiyuan submitted successive memorials exposing Gengyao's crimes; Vice Ministers Shi Yizhi and Gao Qipei went to Shanxi to investigate Shijie's impeachment that Gengyao had sent troops to besiege a civilian fort at Heyang and slaughter the innocent, and also submitted verdicts for deliberation; the emperor ordered separate cases for deliberation on punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Governors and ministers including Yiduli, Fan Shijie, Yue Zhongqi, Tian Wenjing, Huang Bing, Dan Choushu, and Zhao Zhiyuan exposed Gengyao's crimes in successive memorials. Shi Yizhi and Gao Qipei investigated Shijie's charge that Gengyao had besieged a civilian fort at Heyang and slaughtered innocents. The emperor ordered separate deliberations on punishment.

sentences.zh: 罷羹堯將軍，授閒散章京，自二等公遞降至拜他喇布勒哈番，乃盡削羹堯職。

translations.literal: Gengyao was dismissed as general and given an idle clerkship; from second-rank duke his rank was reduced step by step to baitalabule han, and all his offices were then stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao was dismissed as general and given an idle clerkship; his rank fell step by step from second-rank duke to baitalabule han, and all his offices were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 十二月，逮至京師，下議政大臣、三法司、九卿會鞫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was arrested and brought to the capital, and referred to Deliberative Ministers, the Three Judicial Offices, and the Nine Ministers for joint trial.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was arrested and brought to the capital for joint trial by Deliberative Ministers, the Three Judicial Offices, and the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 是月甲戌，具獄辭：羹堯大逆之罪五，欺罔之罪九，僭越之罪十六，狂悖之罪十三，專擅之罪六，忌刻之罪六，殘忍之罪四，貪黷之罪十八，侵蝕之罪十五，凡九十二款，當大辟，親屬緣坐。

translations.literal: On jiaxu of that month the completed case record listed: five counts of great treason, nine of deception, sixteen of overstepping rank, thirteen of reckless impiety, six of monopolizing authority, six of jealousy and harshness, four of cruelty, eighteen of corruption, and fifteen of embezzlement—ninety-two articles in all. The sentence was death by dismemberment, with relatives punished by association.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the indictment listed ninety-two counts: five of great treason, nine of deception, sixteen of overstepping rank, thirteen of reckless impiety, six of monopolizing authority, six of jealousy, four of cruelty, eighteen of corruption, and fifteen of embezzlement. He was sentenced to death by dismemberment, with relatives punished by association.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「羹堯謀逆雖實，而事蹟未著，朕念青海之功，不忍加極刑。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict saying: "Though Gengyao's plotting of rebellion is real, the evidence is not fully established; remembering his Qinghai merit, I cannot bear to inflict the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Though Gengyao's treason is real, the evidence is not fully clear. Remembering his Qinghai service, I cannot bear the extreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 」遣領侍衛內大臣馬爾賽、步軍統領阿齊圖齎詔諭羹堯獄中令自裁。

translations.literal: " He dispatched Chief Bodyguard Grand Minister Ma'ersai and Commander of the Metropolitan Infantry Aqitu bearing an edict to Gengyao in prison ordering him to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Chief Bodyguard Grand Minister Ma'ersai and Commander of the Metropolitan Infantry Aqitu with an edict ordering Gengyao to take his own life in prison.

sentences.zh: 遐齡及羹堯兄希堯奪官，免其罪；

translations.literal: Xialing and Gengyao's elder brother Xiyao were stripped of office but spared punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Xialing and Gengyao's elder brother Xiyao were stripped of office but spared;

sentences.zh: 斬其子富；

translations.literal: his son Fu was beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: his son Fu was executed;

sentences.zh: 諸子年十五以上皆戍極邊。

translations.literal: all sons aged fifteen and above were banished to garrison the extreme frontier.
translations.idiomatic: all sons aged fifteen and above were exiled to the extreme frontier.

sentences.zh: 羹堯幕客鄒魯、汪景祺先後皆坐斬，親屬給披甲為奴。

translations.literal: Gengyao's retainers Zou Lu and Wang Jingqi were both in turn executed by decapitation, and their relatives were given armor and made slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao's retainers Zou Lu and Wang Jingqi were both executed, and their relatives were enslaved as bond servants.

sentences.zh: 又有靜一道人者，四川巡撫憲德捕送京師，亦誅死。

translations.literal: There was also the Daoist Jingyi, whom Sichuan Governor Xiande arrested and sent to the capital; he too was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Jingyi was also arrested by Sichuan Governor Xiande, sent to the capital, and executed.

sentences.zh: 五年，赦羹堯諸子，交遐齡管束。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Gengyao's sons were pardoned and placed under Xialing's discipline.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Gengyao's sons were pardoned and placed under Xialing's supervision.

sentences.zh: 遐齡旋卒，還原職，賜祭。

translations.literal: Xialing soon afterward died; his original rank was restored and sacrificial offerings granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xialing soon died; his original rank was restored and sacrificial rites granted.

sentences.zh: 希堯，初自筆帖式累擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Xiyao, at first rising from clerk, was promoted step by step to vice minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyao rose from clerk to vice minister of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 既，奪官，復起內務府總管，命榷稅淮安，加左都御史。

translations.literal: Afterward he was stripped of office, then reappointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, ordered to levy taxes at Huai'an, and given the rank of left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After dismissal he was reappointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, ordered to levy taxes at Huai'an, and made left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，為江蘇巡撫高其倬劾罷。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was impeached and dismissed by Jiangsu Governor Gao Qizhuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Jiangsu Governor Gao Qizhuo impeached and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 3.

sentences.zh: 胡期恆，字元方，湖廣武陵人。

translations.literal: Hu Qiheng, style name Yuanfang, was a native of Wuling in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qiheng, whose style was Yuanfang, was from Wuling in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 祖統虞，明崇禎末進士。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tongyu was a jinshi in the late Chongzhen reign of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tongyu was a jinshi in late Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 國初授檢討，官至秘書院學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty he was appointed reviser and rose to academician of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he was made reviser and rose to Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 父獻徵，自廕生授都察院經歷，官至湖北布政使。

translations.literal: His father Xianzheng, from a yin privilege appointment as secretary in the Censorate, rose to provincial administration commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianzheng entered through yin privilege as a Censorate secretary and rose to Hubei administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 期恆，康熙四十四年舉人。

translations.literal: Qiheng was a provincial graduate in the forty-fourth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng passed the provincial examinations in Kangxi 44.

sentences.zh: 獻徵與遐齡友，歡若弟昆，期恆少從羹堯遊。

translations.literal: Xianzheng was friends with Xialing, as close as brothers, and Qiheng in his youth associated with Gengyao.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzheng was as close to Xialing as a brother, and Qiheng associated with Gengyao from youth.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，獻詩，授翰林院典籍。

translations.literal: When the emperor made a southern tour, he presented a poem and was appointed Hanlin archivist.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the south, he presented a poem and was appointed Hanlin archivist.

sentences.zh: 出為夔州通判，有恩信，民為建生祠。

translations.literal: He went out as subprefect of Kuizhou, showed kindness and trustworthiness, and the people built a living shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: As subprefect of Kuizhou he won the people's trust, and they built a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 羹堯為巡撫，薦期恆，遷夔州知府，再遷川東道。

translations.literal: When Gengyao was governor he recommended Qiheng, who was transferred to prefect of Kuizhou and then to Eastern Sichuan circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gengyao was governor he recommended Qiheng, who became prefect of Kuizhou and then Eastern Sichuan circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 羹堯兼督陝西，复薦遷陝西布政使。

translations.literal: When Gengyao also supervised Shaanxi, he again recommended Qiheng for transfer to Shaanxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Gengyao also supervised Shaanxi, he again recommended Qiheng as Shaanxi administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 期恆通曉朝章國故，才敏，善理繁劇，羹堯深倚之。

translations.literal: Qiheng was thoroughly versed in court regulations and national affairs, talented and quick, skilled at handling complex and urgent matters, and Gengyao relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng knew court regulations and national affairs thoroughly, was quick and capable with complex business, and Gengyao relied on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 羹堯挾貴而驕，惟期恆能以微言救其失。

translations.literal: Gengyao, relying on his eminence, was arrogant; only Qiheng could with subtle words remedy his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao grew arrogant with power; only Qiheng could correct him with subtle words.

sentences.zh: 羹堯奴辱咸陽知縣，期恆執而杖之，自是諸奴稍斂戢。

translations.literal: Gengyao's slave insulted the magistrate of Xianyang; Qiheng arrested him and had him beaten with the staff, and from then on the slaves somewhat restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Gengyao's slave insulted the magistrate of Xianyang, Qiheng had him arrested and beaten, and the slaves thereafter restrained themselves somewhat.

sentences.zh: 嘗諷羹堯善持盈，羹堯勿能用。

translations.literal: He once admonished Gengyao to know how to hold fullness in balance, but Gengyao would not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: He once urged Gengyao to know when to hold back, but Gengyao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及羹堯敗，諸為羹堯引進者，爭劾羹堯以自解；

translations.literal: When Gengyao fell, all whom he had advanced competed in impeaching him to clear themselves;
translations.idiomatic: When Gengyao fell, all whom he had advanced rushed to impeach him to clear themselves;

sentences.zh: 期恆惟引咎，終不言羹堯，乃下獄頌系。

translations.literal: Qiheng alone took blame upon himself and to the end never spoke against Gengyao; he was imprisoned awaiting trial.
translations.idiomatic: Qiheng alone took the blame and never spoke against Gengyao; he was imprisoned awaiting trial.

sentences.zh: 至高宗即位，始得釋。

translations.literal: Only when the Gaozong Emperor took the throne was he released.
translations.idiomatic: He was released only when the Qianlong Emperor took the throne.

sentences.zh: 僑居江南，久之，卒。

translations.literal: He lived in exile in Jiangnan and, after a long time, died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in exile in Jiangnan and died there long afterward.

sentences.zh: 論曰：雍正初，隆科多以貴戚，年羹堯以戰多，內外夾輔為重臣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: At the beginning of Yongzheng, Long Keduo by imperial kinship and Nian Gengyao by many battles were great ministers supporting the throne within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: At the beginning of Yongzheng, Long Keduo by imperial kinship and Nian Gengyao by battlefield merit were the great ministers supporting the throne at court and in the field.

sentences.zh: 乃不旋踵，幽囚誅夷，亡也忽諸。

translations.literal: Yet in no time they were imprisoned and executed to extinction, perishing all but suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet almost at once they were imprisoned and executed, perishing as suddenly as they had risen.

sentences.zh: 當其貴盛侈汰，隆科多恃元舅之親，受顧命之重；

translations.literal: When they were at the height of honor, splendor, and extravagance, Long Keduo relied on kinship as the emperor's uncle by marriage and the weight of receiving the testament;
translations.idiomatic: At the height of their power and extravagance, Long Keduo relied on his kinship as the emperor's uncle by marriage and on having received the dying emperor's testament;

sentences.zh: 羹堯自代允禵為大將軍，師所向有功。

translations.literal: Gengyao himself replaced Yunsi as great general, and wherever his army went there was merit.
translations.idiomatic: Gengyao had replaced Yunsi as great general, and his armies won victory wherever they marched.

sentences.zh: 方且憑藉權勢，無復顧忌，即於覆滅而不自怵。

translations.literal: They were just then relying on power and influence without further restraint, and even on the verge of ruin did not restrain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They relied on power without restraint and did not check themselves even as ruin approached.

sentences.zh: 臣罔作威福，古聖所誡，可不謹歟！

translations.literal: Ministers must not arrogate authority and bestow favors—the ancient sages warned of this. How can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Ministers must not arrogate authority and bestow favors—the ancient sages warned of this. How can one not take heed!
